new.title: NAV-anchored exit floor lets an unprivileged actor cheaply revert a pending exit, skim, or totalWithdrawal Phase-2 by front-running with a Curve pool dump (transient griefing)
new.decision: PARTIAL MATCH, kept (rule: when in doubt keep). Same NAV-anchored minOut code path as two false-positive entries, but a different harm class. M-02 d7f6c2dfd580 was closed as a VALUE-LEAK framing. Its triageNote reads: 'the design allows in-block swaps without MEV fear precisely because the AMM pool is concentrated liquidity ... No valid attack path.' M-02-run11 c7329862eb0e was closed as persistent Withdraw-DoS. Its suppressionReason reads: 'Withdraw-DoS requires the AMM/vault price to decouple and stay decoupled -- closed by arbitrage and prevented by the NG rate oracle.' DEDUP-18-04 claims neither a leak nor a persistent decouple. It is a transient, same-bundle front-run revert grief. A fork probe shows ~23.8 bps live headroom under a 30 bps tolerance and a ~$127 griefing cost. Arbitrage cannot close a same-bundle push. Neither closure's rationale addresses this. Re-filed with disclosure. It must NOT be framed as a value leak or a solvency issue (doNotReRaise).
disclose: fdda8f53151a M-01-run12 false-positive (realizable-solvency framing; do not re-raise)
new.flagForHuman: Owner previously rejected MEV framings on this path. Confirm a QA-level revert-grief note is wanted.

Not suppressible by the minter-cushion or opportunity-cost memories: the static 1.38 bps autoUSD discount is accepted design, but the manipulable leg is UNVERIFIED. Medium trigger: a fork probe shows autoUSD redeem delivery depressible by more than ~10 bps at a cost below the extracted top-up.
